The package would let liquidators and the Australian Securities and Investments Commission reclaim property transferred in a way that defeats creditors. The new criminal offences cover company officers who arrange such transfers and anyone who encourages them, with a strict liability offence for ignoring an ASIC recovery order.. Company officers, persons who encourage creditor-defeating transfers, and liquidators and ASIC who enforce recovery of transferred property.

title: National Health Amendment (Pharmaceutical Benefits) Bill 2019
snippet: lapsed. Health. The bill would change how the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme handles pharmacy approvals and medicine supply after pharmacy insolvency. It would introduce a fee for pharmacists applying to supply PBS medicines and let the Minister set the fee by regulation. The bill would also let the Health Secretary temporarily allow a bankruptcy trustee to keep supplying PBS medicines at a bankrupt pharmacy until it is sold.. Pharmacists, bankruptcy trustees, external administrators, and consumers who rely on PBS medicines at affected pharmacies.

title: Treasury Laws Amendment (Registries Modernisation and Other Measures) Bill 2019
snippet: lapsed. Treasury. This bill is part of a package that would modernise Commonwealth business registers and introduce a director identification number requirement. The package would allow a minister to appoint an existing Commonwealth body as registrar, with powers and functions set out in existing laws and data standards made by the registrar. Directors of bodies registered under the Corporations Act or CATSI Act would need to apply for a director identification number before appointment, with transitional arrangements for current directors.. Directors of bodies registered under the Corporations Act or CATSI Act, and the registrar appointed to administer the new regime.
